- Mimic eggs disguised as gold coins spread through Stickyickistan.
- The [[Tribunal Highblade Coalition]] hires the party to escort a caravan through the reopened route.
- A strange route beneath the forest leads toward [[Doobius House]] or the deeper Outback.

## Rewards

| Hunt Level | Restoring Safety to the Neck | Finding Stein’s Brother | XP |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 3rd | 250 gp per character | 125 gp per character | 600 per character |
| 8th | 1,250 gp per character | 550 gp per character | 3,900 per character |
| 13th | 3,500 gp per character | 1,500 gp per character | 10,000 per character |

The tavern’s remains contain coins and preserved monster components. Use the following amounts:

| Hunt Level | Coins | Monster Components |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 3rd | 3d6 × 50 gp | 2 components and fragile essence |
| 8th | 3d6 × 100 gp | 3 components and robust essence |
| 13th | 3d6 × 200 gp | 4 components and potent essence |

## Harvesting

The Tanglepine Terror provides the normal components for a monstrosity, plus unique materials that can be harvested from its mimic body and Jonjo’s central nervous system:

| DC | Components |
|---:|---|
| 10 | Pouch of teeth |
| 15 | Tongue and stomach |
| 20 | Brain and skin |

A successful DC 12 Intelligence (Nature) check identifies acid damage on the bones and metal. A successful DC 14 Wisdom (Medicine) check reveals that the pile contains no bones from the ankle downward, suggesting the victims’ feet were removed and used by the creature as locomotion.

### Clue 2: The Tavern Mimic

The Tanglepine Terror disguises itself as a warm, welcoming roadside tavern. When it moves, hundreds of mismatched feet sprout from its underside and trample the forest.

A successful DC 14 Wisdom (Survival) check identifies that the hundreds of footprints are humanoid and all face away from the rectangular outline of the creature.

### Clue 3: Warded Exterior

Dr. Stein’s wards prevent the Tanglepine Terror from being harmed from outside. Spells, weapons, and flames are deflected or redirected. The characters must enter the tavern to damage its inhabitants and central nervous system.

### Guthric

Guthric is an alignment-good human commoner and former caravaneer’s apprentice. He hides near one of the clearings and approaches the party if he hears them discussing the monster.

Guthric explains that his caravan stopped outside the tavern because the guards could not afford an inn. The guards entered after hearing screams but never returned. Guthric threw alchemist’s fire at the building, but the flames were deflected and burned the ground instead.

## The Battle Ahead

The tavern mimic is both monster and lair. The characters can only harm it by entering the building and fighting from within.

The party faces three consecutive waves:

1. Furniture and smaller mimics.
2. A shrinking effect that places the characters on a gigantic dinner table.
3. Jonjo Starr’s tavern-mimic form and its central nervous system.

Track damage toward the wave thresholds rather than reducing the tavern mimic’s hit points normally.

### Wave Damage Thresholds

| Hunt Level | Wave 1 | Wave 2 |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 3rd | 90 | 180 |
| 8th | 230 | 460 |
| 13th | 350 | 700 |

Areas of effect and ongoing damage count only once per round toward a threshold, using the highest simultaneous instance of damage.

## A Tavern’s Domain

The Tanglepine Terror establishes itself at a busy crossroads or isolated section of the Neck. The surrounding six miles show signs of its presence:

- Hundreds of mismatched footprints cross the road.
- Piles of bleached bones and untarnished metal appear beneath the trees.
- Travelers tell stories about an innkeeper whose patrons all speak and move alike.
- Other taverns along the Neck have begun refusing travelers after dark.

### Lair Actions

While the Tanglepine Terror lives, it can use the following lair actions on initiative count 20. It cannot use the same action two rounds in a row.

| Hunt Level | VDC | Vdam |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 3rd | 12 | 3 (1d6) |
| 8th | 14 | 7 (2d6) |
| 13th | 16 | 14 (4d6) |

- **Drool:** Acid falls on a 30-foot square. Creatures beneath it make a Dexterity saving throw, taking Vdam acid damage on a failure or half damage on a success.
- **Peristalsis:** The tavern contracts. Each non-mimic creature inside makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, it is pushed 15 feet, falls prone, and takes Vdam bludgeoning damage. On a success, it moves 5 feet without falling or taking damage.
- **Sink:** A 10-foot square of floor becomes sticky and soft. Creatures in the area make a Strength saving throw or become restrained. A restrained creature sinks 2 feet at the end of its turn and takes Vdam acid damage.

## Entering the Tavern

When the characters reach the tavern, read or paraphrase:

> Laughter spills from a warmly lit wooden building in a forest clearing. Silhouettes of drinkers move behind sackcloth curtains, and hundreds of different footprints lead to the walls before stopping abruptly.

Inside, read or paraphrase:

> A dozen patrons laugh around a smokeless fire while a landlady raises filled tankards over the bar. The air is cold and stale despite the hearth.
>
> “New customers!” she says with an unblinking smile. “First one’s on the house.”

The tankards contain acid. A creature that drinks takes Vdam acid damage.

The door seals after the characters enter. Characters notice the tavern is unnatural if they investigate the repeating gestures, fixed smiles, cold fire, or eyes appearing briefly in the walls.

## Wave 1: Furniture

If the characters act aggressively or try to leave, the smaller mimics attack.

- **3rd level:** 1 Mimic and 2 Swarms of Mimics.
- **8th level:** 1 Mimic, 1 Mirror Mimic, and 2 Swarms of Mimics.
- **13th level:** 2 Mirror Mimics and 4 Mimics.

Use official stat blocks for Mimics and other published mimic creatures available to the DM. The mimics use the tavern’s furniture, walls, and patrons as cover.

## Wave 2: Shrink

When the Wave 1 damage threshold is reached, the tavern shrinks the characters and their equipment to roughly 2 inches tall and places them on a huge table. The table’s cutlery, coins, cups, and food become the battlefield.

Read or paraphrase:

> The tavern lurches. The table rises around you, stretching into a towering landscape. Cups become wells, forks become iron bars, and a smear of purple sauce lies two feet deep across the tabletop.
>
> Then the cutlery moves.

- **3rd level:** 4 Mimics with half their normal hit points.
- **8th level:** 5 high-threat Mimics and 2 standard Mimics.
- **13th level:** 3 Mirror Mimics and 3 high-threat Mimics.

When the Wave 2 threshold is reached, the characters return to normal size.

## Wave 3: Jonjo Starr

Jonjo’s face extrudes from the tavern wall as the Tanglepine Terror reveals its central nervous system.

Read or paraphrase:

> The table vanishes and the world snaps back to its proper scale. A humanoid face pushes through the tavern wall, stretched across pale lilac strands.
>
> The building shudders around you.
>
> “You’re proving to be quite the nuisance.”

The characters may fight Jonjo’s tavern-mimic form or use Dr. Stein’s biomatter transponder. If a character spends an action operating the device for three consecutive rounds, Dr. Stein appears and traps Jonjo in a magical locket, ending the encounter.

### Wave 3 Enemies

- **3rd level:** 1 Emaciated Tavern Mimic Brain and 1 Mimic.
- **8th level:** 1 Tavern Mimic Brain and 1 Mirror Mimic.
- **13th level:** 1 Nourished Tavern Mimic Brain and 2 Mirror Mimics.

Use the appropriate official stat blocks from the adventure’s source material. The central nervous system is part of the tavern mimic and transfers damage to the main creature.

## Optional Ending: Digestif

When Jonjo is defeated or captured, the tavern begins to collapse. Acid fills the interior, the floor becomes difficult terrain, and the structure folds inward.

At initiative count 0, the tavern fills with 1 foot of acid. Each creature still inside takes Vdam acid damage for each foot of acid. At the end of the third round, the tavern collapses.

# Aftermath

Dr. Stein pays the agreed compensation and, if Jonjo is saved, offers to teach one biomancy spell to a wizard in the party.

The [[Nevercough Tribunal]] reopens the Neck once the Tanglepine Terror is gone. Merchants and caravans begin using the route again, though travelers continue to avoid roadside taverns for several months.

The Tanglepines remain dangerous. Dr. Stein’s escaped experiments, mimics, and altered plants provide future hunting contracts.

## Further Adventure Hooks

- Dr. Stein’s wards fail, allowing chimeric creatures to reach North Booftown.
- A new roadside inn appears on the Neck, but nobody remembers building it.
- Mimic eggs disguised as gold coins spread through Stickyickistan.
- The [[Tribunal Highblade Coalition]] hires the party to escort a caravan through the reopened route.
- A strange route beneath the forest leads toward [[Doobius House]] or the deeper Outback.

## Rewards

| Hunt Level | Restoring Safety to the Neck | Finding Stein’s Brother | XP |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 3rd | 250 gp per character | 125 gp per character | 600 per character |
| 8th | 1,250 gp per character | 550 gp per character | 3,900 per character |
| 13th | 3,500 gp per character | 1,500 gp per character | 10,000 per character |

The tavern’s remains contain coins and preserved monster components. Use the following amounts:

| Hunt Level | Coins | Monster Components |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 3rd | 3d6 × 50 gp | 2 components and fragile essence |
| 8th | 3d6 × 100 gp | 3 components and robust essence |
| 13th | 3d6 × 200 gp | 4 components and potent essence |

## Harvesting

The Tanglepine Terror provides the normal components for a monstrosity, plus unique materials that can be harvested from its mimic body and Jonjo’s central nervous system:

| DC | Components |
|---:|---|
| 10 | Pouch of teeth |
| 15 | Tongue and stomach |
| 20 | Brain and skin |

The remains also contain a [[Mimickey]], which can be preserved and socketed onto a held or worn item if the DM uses that optional crafting rule.

2. A shrinking effect that places the characters on a gigantic dinner table.
3. Jonjo Starr’s tavern-mimic form and its central nervous system.

### Wave Damage Thresholds

| Hunt Level | Wave 1 | Wave 2 |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 3rd | 90 | 180 |
| 8th | 230 | 460 |
| 13th | 350 | 700 |

## A Tavern’s Domain

The Tanglepine Terror establishes itself at a busy crossroads or isolated section of the Neck. The surrounding six miles show signs of its presence:

| Hunt Level | VDC | Vdam |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 3rd | 12 | 3 (1d6) |
| 8th | 14 | 7 (2d6) |
| 13th | 16 | 14 (4d6) |

> Laughter spills from a warmly lit wooden building in a forest clearing. Silhouettes of drinkers move behind sackcloth curtains, and hundreds of different footprints lead to the walls before stopping abruptly.

Inside, read or paraphrase:

>

- **8th level:** 1 Mimic, 1 Mirror Mimic, and 2 Swarms of Mimics.
- **13th level:** 2 Mirror Mimics and 4 Mimics.

>
> Then the cutlery moves.

>

>

| Hunt Level | Restoring Safety to the Neck | Finding Stein’s Brother | XP |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 3rd | 250 gp per character | 125 gp per character | 600 per character |
| 8th | 1,250 gp per character | 550 gp per character | 3,900 per character |
| 13th | 3,500 gp per character | 1,500 gp per character | 10,000 per character |

| Hunt Level | Coins | Monster Components |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 3rd | 3d6 × 50 gp | 2 components and fragile essence |
| 8th | 3d6 × 100 gp | 3 components and robust essence |
| 13th | 3d6 × 200 gp | 4 components and potent essence |

| DC | Components |
|---:|---|
| 10 | Pouch of teeth |
| 15 | Tongue and stomach |

| 13th | 350 | 700 |

| 3rd | 12 | 3 (1d6) |
| 8th | 14 | 7 (2d6) |
| 13th | 16 | 14 (4d6) |

- **Peristalsis:** The tavern contracts. Each non-mimic creature inside makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, it is pushed 15 feet, falls prone, and takes Vdam bludgeoning damage. On a success, it moves 5 feet without falling or taking damage.

> Laughter spills from a warmly lit wooden building in a forest clearing. Silhouettes of drinkers move behind sackcloth curtains, and hundreds of different footprints lead to the walls before stopping abruptly.

Inside, read or paraphrase:

> A dozen patrons laugh around a smokeless fire while a landlady raises filled tankards over the bar. The air is cold and stale despite the hearth.
>

- **13th level:** 2 Mirror Mimics and 4 Mimics.

>

>

>

| Hunt Level | Restoring Safety to the Neck | Finding Stein’s Brother | XP |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 3rd | 250 gp per character | 125 gp per character | 600 per character |
| 8th | 1,250 gp per character | 550 gp per character | 3,900 per character |
| 13th | 3,500 gp per character | 1,500 gp per character | 10,000 per character |

| Hunt Level | Coins | Monster Components |
|---:|---:|---:|

| 8th | 3d6 × 100 gp | 3 components and robust essence |
| 13th | 3d6 × 200 gp | 4 components and potent essence |

| DC | Components |

### Lair Actions

While the Tanglepine Terror lives, it can use the following lair actions on initiative count 20. It cannot use the same action two rounds in a row.

| Hunt Level | VDC | Vdam |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 3rd | 12 | 3 (1d6) |
| 8th | 14 | 7 (2d6) |
| 13th | 16 | 14 (4d6) |

- **Drool:** Acid falls on a 30-foot square. Creatures beneath it make a Dexterity saving throw, taking Vdam acid damage on a failure or half damage on a success.
- **Peristalsis:** The tavern contracts. Each non-mimic creature inside makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, it is pushed 15 feet, falls prone, and takes Vdam bludgeoning damage. On a success, it moves 5 feet without falling or taking damage.
- **Sink:** A 10-foot square of floor becomes sticky and soft. Creatures in the area make a Strength saving throw or become restrained. A restrained creature sinks 2 feet at the end of its turn and takes Vdam acid damage.

## Entering the Tavern

When the characters reach the tavern, read or paraphrase:

> Laughter spills from a warmly lit wooden building in a forest clearing. Silhouettes of drinkers move behind sackcloth curtains, and hundreds of different footprints lead to the walls before stopping abruptly.

Inside, read or paraphrase:

> A dozen patrons laugh around a smokeless fire while a landlady raises filled tankards over the bar. The air is cold and stale despite the hearth.
>
> “New customers!” she says with an unblinking smile. “First one’s on the house.”

The tankards contain acid. A creature that drinks takes Vdam acid damage.

The door seals after the characters enter. Characters notice the tavern is unnatural if they investigate the repeating gestures, fixed smiles, cold fire, or eyes appearing briefly in the walls.

## Wave 1: Furniture

If the characters act aggressively or try to leave, the smaller mimics attack.

- **3rd level:** 1 Mimic and 2 Swarms of Mimics.
- **8th level:** 1 Mimic, 1 Mirror Mimic, and 2 Swarms of Mimics.
- **13th level:** 2 Mirror Mimics and 4 Mimics.

Use official stat blocks for Mimics and other published mimic creatures available to the DM. The mimics use the tavern’s furniture, walls, and patrons as cover.

## Wave 2: Shrink

When the Wave 1 damage threshold is reached, the tavern shrinks the characters and their equipment to roughly 2 inches tall and places them on a huge table. The table’s cutlery, coins, cups, and food become the battlefield.

Read or paraphrase:

> The tavern lurches. The table rises around you, stretching into a towering landscape. Cups become wells, forks become iron bars, and a smear of purple sauce lies two feet deep across the tabletop.
>
> Then the cutlery moves.

- **3rd level:** 4 Mimics with half their normal hit points.
- **8th level:** 5 high-threat Mimics and 2 standard Mimics.
- **13th level:** 3 Mirror Mimics and 3 high-threat Mimics.

When the Wave 2 threshold is reached, the characters return to normal size.

## Wave 3: Jonjo Starr

Jonjo’s face extrudes from the tavern wall as the Tanglepine Terror reveals its central nervous system.

Read or paraphrase:

> The table vanishes and the world snaps back to its proper scale. A humanoid face pushes through the tavern wall, stretched across pale lilac strands.
>
> The building shudders around you.
>
> “You’re proving to be quite the nuisance.”

The characters may fight Jonjo’s tavern-mimic form or use Dr. Stein’s biomatter transponder. If a character spends an action operating the device for three consecutive rounds, Dr. Stein appears and traps Jonjo in a magical locket, ending the encounter.

### Wave 3 Enemies

- **3rd level:** 1 Emaciated Tavern Mimic Brain and 1 Mimic.
- **8th level:** 1 Tavern Mimic Brain and 1 Mirror Mimic.
- **13th level:** 1 Nourished Tavern Mimic Brain and 2 Mirror Mimics.

Use the appropriate official stat blocks from the adventure’s source material. The central nervous system is part of the tavern mimic and transfers damage to the main creature.

## Optional Ending: Digestif

When Jonjo is defeated or captured, the tavern begins to collapse. Acid fills the interior, the floor becomes difficult terrain, and the structure folds inward.

At initiative count 0, the tavern fills with 1 foot of acid. Each creature still inside takes Vdam acid damage for each foot of acid. At the end of the third round, the tavern collapses.

# Aftermath

Dr. Stein pays the agreed compensation and, if Jonjo is saved, offers to teach one biomancy spell to a wizard in the party.

The [[Nevercough Tribunal]] reopens the Neck once the Grim Forest Terror is gone. Merchants and caravans begin using the route again, though travelers continue to avoid roadside taverns for several months.

The Grim Forest remains dangerous. Dr. Stein’s escaped experiments, mimics, and altered plants provide future hunting contracts.

## Further Adventure Hooks

- Dr. Stein’s wards fail, allowing chimeric creatures to reach North Booftown.
- A new roadside inn appears on the Neck, but nobody remembers building it.
- Mimic eggs disguised as gold coins spread through Stickyickistan.
- The [[Tribunal Highblade Coalition]] hires the party to escort a caravan through the reopened route.
- A strange route beneath the forest leads toward [[Doobius House]] or the deeper Outback.

## Rewards

| Hunt Level | Restoring Safety to the Neck | Finding Stein’s Brother | XP |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 3rd | 250 gp per character | 125 gp per character | 600 per character |
| 8th | 1,250 gp per character | 550 gp per character | 3,900 per character |
| 13th | 3,500 gp per character | 1,500 gp per character | 10,000 per character |

The tavern’s remains contain coins and preserved monster components. Use the following amounts:

| Hunt Level | Coins | Monster Components |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 3rd | 3d6 × 50 gp | 2 components and fragile essence |
| 8th | 3d6 × 100 gp | 3 components and robust essence |
| 13th | 3d6 × 200 gp | 4 components and potent essence |

## Harvesting

The Tanglepine Terror provides the normal components for a monstrosity, plus unique materials that can be harvested from its mimic body and Jonjo’s central nervous system:

| DC | Components |
|---:|---|
| 10 | Pouch of teeth |
| 15 | Tongue and stomach |
| 20 | Brain and skin |

The remains also contain a [[Mimickey]], which can be preserved and socketed onto a held or worn item if the DM uses that optional crafting rule.

# Dr. Francis Norman Stein

Dr. Francis Norman Stein is a brilliant, distracted, and deeply irresponsible biomancy wizard whose experiments have reshaped parts of [[The Outback]]. His work combines arcane engineering, biological augmentation, and experimental creature design. The results are often impressive, frequently dangerous, and rarely approved by the [[Nevercough Tribunal]].

Stein is best known for creating strange chimeras, unstable constructs, and self-sustaining magical systems. He insists that most accidents are simply “unexpected data.” His body is now more arcane life-support system than flesh, sustained by a network of Magitech components, alchemical reservoirs, and magical prosthetics.

## Role in Stickyickistan

Stein operates from concealed laboratories and temporary workshops rather than a permanent public institution. His experiments have contributed to the magical contamination and unusual wildlife found in the [[Grim Forest]]. Although he has attempted to control the damage with wards, containment fields, and redirected growth patterns, his safeguards are unreliable and often create new problems.

The [[Ashen Shadow Society]], the [[Tribunal Highblade Coalition]], independent researchers, and wealthy industrialists have all sought Stein’s expertise at one time or another. Many of them regret the arrangement, but few deny that his inventions work.

## Appearance

Stein is a thin, elderly Human wizard whose remaining organic features are surrounded by brass fittings, glass tubes, insulated cables, and articulated Magitech braces. His voice occasionally cuts out, emits a burst of static, or is replaced by the hiss of a pressure valve.

He wears a stained laboratory coat beneath a heavy traveling cloak. His pockets contain notebooks, surgical tools, incomplete diagrams, unstable samples, and objects he has forgotten are dangerous.

## Personality

- Brilliant but easily distracted.
- Treats ethical concerns as logistical obstacles.
- Speaks in technical language even when simple words would suffice.
- Views monsters as research opportunities before recognizing them as threats.
- Genuinely cares about his creations, though he rarely understands what they need.
- Becomes defensive when anyone describes his work as irresponsible.

## Motivations

Stein wants to understand life, death, transformation, and the creation of artificial organisms. He is especially interested in preserving consciousness through biological and mechanical means.

He also wants to recover lost research, reclaim abandoned laboratories, and prove that his work can be controlled. The disappearance of his brother, [[Jonjo Starr]], is complicated by Stein’s guilt and professional curiosity. He wants Jonjo found, but he is also fascinated by what Jonjo became.

## Relationship with Jonjo Starr

Jonjo Starr was Stein’s half-brother and an amateur wizard who attempted to create a phylactery. During the ritual, Jonjo mistook a mimic for a perpetually refilling amphora. The resulting magical accident fused Jonjo, the mimic, and part of Stein’s laboratory into the **Grim Forest Terror**.

Stein considers the Grim Forest Terror both a family tragedy and a remarkable scientific development. He would prefer Jonjo recovered alive or intact enough to study, but he accepts that destroying the creature may be necessary.

## Adventure Hooks

- Stein hires adventurers to investigate a monster created by one of his failed experiments.
- He offers payment for recovering lost laboratory equipment from [[The Outback]].
- A dangerous creature escapes from one of his containment sites.
- Stein needs test subjects for a harmless experiment, though his definition of harmless is unreliable.
- He wants the party to retrieve [[Jonjo Starr]] or destroy the Grim Forest Terror.
- He offers a rare spell, magical device, or experimental component in exchange for field data.

## Mannerisms and Sayings

- Takes notes during conversations and occasionally forgets the person is still speaking.
- Adjusts a valve on his neck whenever he is excited.
- Refers to explosions as “rapid unscheduled releases of energy.”
- Calls monsters “uncooperative research partners.”
- Pauses mid-sentence to record a new hypothesis.

> “A dangerous experiment is merely an experiment that has begun collecting its own evidence.”

> “I have not lost my laboratory. It has simply become mobile, hostile, and difficult to locate.”

The relationship is now transactional and cautious: professors request his help through sealed correspondence, while Stein borrows equipment, cites restricted papers, and recruits students who are willing to accompany him into the field. Some faculty members want his work preserved, while others believe he should be permanently barred from every laboratory in Stickyickistan.

# Adventure Summary

**Dread and Breakfast** is a monster-hunt adventure set in the [[Grim Forest]], a dangerous woodland within [[The Outback]] of [[Stickyickistan]]. Travelers and caravans have begun disappearing along the Neck, a trade route connecting [[North Booftown]] with inland settlements such as [[Doobius House]]. The characters are hired to investigate the disappearances and uncover the truth behind a welcoming roadside tavern that is far more alive than it appears.

The adventure culminates in a three-wave encounter inside a tavern mimic. Characters should be prepared for a strange, dangerous fight involving smaller mimics, shrinking magic, acid, and a creature that cannot be harmed from outside.

# The Rolling Papers Advertisement

**Submitted by:** [[The Nevercough Tribunal]] and Dr. Stein  
**Tier:** Tier 1  
**Recommended Level:** 3  
**Expected Length:** One-shot, approximately 3–4 hours  
**Tone:** Forest horror, monster investigation, biomantic weirdness, dark comedy  
**Location:** [[Grim Forest]] / The Neck  

## Headline

> **TRAVELERS MISSING ALONG THE NECK: LICENSED HUNTERS REQUESTED**

## Public Notice

Caravans and travelers have disappeared along the trade route through the [[Grim Forest]]. The [[Nevercough Tribunal]] seeks capable adventurers to investigate the disappearances, protect future caravans, and remove the creature responsible.

Dr. Stein offers additional compensation for the recovery of his missing laboratory or the safe return of his half-brother, [[Jonjo Starr]].

Applicants should report to the northern road station at the edge of the Grim Forest. Ask for the biomancy researcher with the metal lungs.

# What Players Should Know

- **Content / vibe:** Forest horror, missing travelers, acid, body horror, biomantic experiments, mimics, and dark comedy.
- **Combat / roleplay / exploration mix:** Investigation and tracking followed by a dangerous three-wave combat encounter.
- **Character hooks:** Good for monster hunters, caravan guards, Free League contractors, researchers, bounty hunters, or adventurers seeking payment and unusual monster components.
- **Special notes:** The party will investigate the Grim Forest, track the creature along the Neck, and enter a tavern mimic to fight it from within. Expect little downtime between combat waves.

# Character Creation

- Create a **3rd-level** character.
- Use the character creation rules in [[Character Building]].
- Any official species, class, or background is welcome. Stickyickistan is home to species from across the multiverse.
- Use standard array or roll ability scores before the session. If you do not roll beforehand, use standard array.
- Use fixed hit points when gaining levels.
- Choose a non-evil alignment.
- Your character should have a reason to accept monster-hunting or caravan-protection work and cooperate with the rest of the party.
- Consult the DM before bringing your character to the table. The DM has final approval over character options and concepts.

## Starting Equipment

Your 3rd-level character begins with:

- Normal starting equipment and gold.
- An additional 250 gp.
- One uncommon magic item.
- One common magic item.
- One uncommon [[Arcannabis]] zip.

Potions count as your uncommon magic item. Do not use deprecated homebrew magic items labeled “Arcannabis” on D&D Beyond. Use the current Arcannabis options approved by the DM.

## Stickyickistanian Backgrounds

Choose one of the following connections or create your own:

- A member or contractor of the [[Ashen Shadow Society]], a bounty-hunting guild that collects bounties, relics, and monster components. Characters associated with the Society are generally lawful neutral and cannot be evil-aligned.
- An employee or associate of [[The Seekers of the Vein]], a mining and jeweler’s guild with interests in rare magical materials.
- A member of the [[Tribunal Highblade Coalition]], a lawful mercenary organization operating throughout Stickyickistan.
- A caravan guard, merchant, or traveler who regularly uses the Neck.
- A researcher or former student connected to Dr. Stein or [[N.E.R.D]].
- A resident of [[North Booftown]] or [[Doobius House]] who wants to protect the trade route.
- A monster hunter responding to the public notice in [[The Rolling Papers]].

## Setting Context

- [[Stickyickistan]] is a magical island city-state dominated by the active volcano [[Mount Zooka]].
- [[The Outback]] is a vast wilderness beyond the city containing ruins, monsters, magical anomalies, and isolated settlements.
- [[Grim Forest]] is a dangerous forest within The Outback, shaped by colonial logging, old battlefields, magical contamination, and abandoned war machines.
- The Neck is a major trade route connecting [[North Booftown]] with inland settlements such as [[Doobius House]].
- The [[Nevercough Tribunal]] wants the route kept open, while Dr. Stein wants his missing laboratory and brother recovered.
- Mimics, biomantic experiments, and escaped creatures are known dangers in the region.

## Useful Skills

Characters proficient in the following skills may find opportunities to contribute:

- Arcana
- Investigation
- Medicine
- Nature
- Perception
- Survival

Acid resistance, healing, control effects, and abilities that help with confined spaces may be especially useful.

## What Characters Know

Before play begins, characters know the following:

- Travelers and caravans have disappeared along the Neck.
- A strange roadside tavern has been seen near recent disappearances.
- Survivors report identical patrons, cold fires, and an innkeeper with an unnatural smile.
- Dr. Stein’s laboratory and half-brother, [[Jonjo Starr]], are also missing.
- The public contract offers payment for restoring safety to the route and additional compensation for finding Jonjo.
- The creature may not be vulnerable to attacks made from outside the tavern.

## Character Hooks

Your character might:

- Have answered the public notice in [[The Rolling Papers]].
- Be responsible for protecting a caravan traveling along the Neck.
- Know someone who disappeared in the Grim Forest.
- Have professional or personal ties to Dr. Stein, [[N.E.R.D]], the [[Ashen Shadow Society]], or the [[Nevercough Tribunal]].
- Want to study mimics, biomancy, or unusual monster components.
- Be seeking payment, fame, or future work from the Tribunal or Free League.

# Rewards

- **250 gp per character** for restoring safety to the Neck.
- **125 gp per character** for finding Dr. Stein’s brother.
- XP from the adventure’s encounters.
- Additional coins and monster components from the tavern mimic.
- Possible future work from Dr. Stein, the [[Nevercough Tribunal]], or the [[Tribunal Highblade Coalition]].
- The opportunity to harvest unusual mimic components for crafting.

# Sign-Up

**DM:** TBD  
**Date / Time:** TBD  
**Seats:** 4–5 players  
**How to join:** Register through the [[FLS Guildhall]] or post in the Free League chat.

*A Stickyickistan Adventure for Four to Five 3rd-Level Characters*

Crimson Candleworks is optimized for five 3rd-level characters. This adventure should be completed in four hours or less.

The adventure takes place in the city of [[Stickyickistan]], where a seemingly ordinary candle maker's workshop conceals an illegal Bloodwalker OG distribution operation beneath its floorboards. Hired by the [[Tribunal Highblade Coalition]], the characters investigate the business, uncover its hidden cellar, and dismantle the criminal enterprise operating below.

# Intro

## Adjusting Encounters

If you have fewer than five players, a group of inexperienced players, or characters who are poorly equipped, the adventure may suggest adjusting certain encounters to be less challenging. If your players are experienced or have particularly optimized characters, the adventure may also suggest ways to increase the difficulty.

Consult with your players before beginning if adjustments seem appropriate. You can always modify encounters during play to provide the most enjoyable experience for your table.

---

## Key Plot Points

The following information is key to the adventure's story.

**Part 1:** [[The Rolling Papers]]. The characters discover a bounty posted by the Tribunal Highblade Coalition seeking adventurers willing to raid a suspected Bloodwalker OG distribution site operating beneath a candle maker's workshop.

**Part 2:** Wick & Wax Candleworks. The characters investigate the workshop, discover the concealed trapdoor hidden beneath a worn rug, and descend into the cellar where the operation is based. There they confront the undead traffickers responsible for distributing the illegal strain.

**Conclusion:** Another Candle Extinguished. After dismantling the operation, the characters recover evidence pointing toward the unknown producers of Bloodwalker OG before returning to the Tribunal Highblade Coalition to claim their reward.

---

## Preparation

Before running the adventure, prepare as follows:

- **Step 1**. Read the Adventure Background section.
- **Step 2**. Review any rules from the Player's Handbook, Dungeon Master's Guide, or Homebrew that may come into play.
- **Step 3**. Bookmark the creature stat blocks needed for the adventure or have them readily available.
- **Step 4.** Familiarize yourself with the [[Arcannabis System Rework]], and the Cooking rules in [[Heliana's Guide to Monster Hunting]], so you know why and how Bloodwalker OG works the way it does.

The following stat blocks are used in this adventure:

- [[Apprentice Vamplock]]
- [[Cultist]]
- [[Shadow]]
- [[Vampirate Mage]]

> [!Read Aloud]
> Text that appears in a box like this is intended to be read aloud or paraphrased for the players when their characters first arrive at a location or under the circumstances described.

---

## Key NPCs

|                      |                                                                                                                      |                       |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| Name                 | Role                                                                                                                 | Stat Block            |
| [[Ziggy Tootokes]]   | Coalition agent overseeing the bounty                                                                                | Level 3 Rogue (Scout) |
| [[Marek Flint]]      | Manager of the Wick & Wax Candleshop. Also a member of a gang called The Bloodline. He leads this distribution cell. | Vampirate Mage        |
| Apprentice Vamplocks | Undead assistants managing the cellar                                                                                | Apprentice Vamplock   |

---

## Content Warning

Body horror, illicit drug trafficking, undead, murder, and references to harvested humanoid remains.

---

## Adventure Background

[[Arcannabis]] has long been one of Stickyickistan's most valuable commodities. While legitimate growers operate under strict regulations, criminal organizations continue to produce illicit strains using dangerous and prohibited ingredients.

Among the most infamous is [[Bloodwalker OG]], a strain outlawed by the [[Stickyickistanian Department of Public Health]] after investigators discovered it was manufactured using harvested humanoid hearts, celestial remains, and other forbidden monster components.

Responsibility for enforcing that ban falls to the [[Tribunal Highblade Coalition]] (THC). For months, Coalition investigators have pursued dealers distributing Bloodwalker OG throughout the city, but every trail has ended before reaching the source.

Their investigation finally uncovered a consistent pattern. Couriers supplying local dealers repeatedly visited an aging candle maker's workshop tucked away among the city's older commercial district. Although the storefront appeared to conduct legitimate business during the day, surveillance revealed unusual deliveries after dark and an impossible amount of traffic for a struggling artisan.

Unable to obtain sufficient evidence for a lawful raid, Coalition investigators posted a public bounty seeking capable adventurers willing to investigate the property.

Unknown to the authorities, the candle workshop serves as little more than a façade. Beneath a faded rug inside the workshop lies a concealed trapdoor leading into a cellar where Bloodwalker OG is packaged, stored, and distributed throughout the city. Shipments arrive from hidden cultivation sites elsewhere in Stickyickistan, while victims murdered during the operation have their hearts harvested and returned to the growers for future production.

The cellar is commanded by a Vampirate and several undead accomplices, all of whom have consumed Bloodwalker OG and now zealously protect the operation. If the workshop is exposed, the Coalition hopes the evidence recovered below will reveal who truly controls the Bloodwalker OG supply.

---

# Part 1: The Rolling Papers
*Estimated Duration: 30 Minutes*

In this part, the characters discover a bounty advertisement in The Rolling Papers, Stickyickistan's most widely circulated newspaper. Reporting to the Tribunal Highblade Coalition (THC), they meet Investigator Ziggy Tootokes, who briefs them on an ongoing Bloodwalker OG investigation before sending them to raid a suspected distribution site concealed beneath a candle maker's workshop.

## Adventure Hook

While reading the latest edition of The Rolling Papers, the characters notice a bounty posted in the newspaper's Bounties & Advertisements section.

Hand the players the following notice or read it aloud.

---

### BOUNTY POSTED

#### Tribunal Highblade Coalition

INVESTIGATION & RAID AUTHORIZED

The Tribunal Highblade Coalition seeks capable adventurers to investigate a suspected illegal Arcannabis distribution operation believed to be beneath Wick & Wax Candleworks, located in the [[Old Market District]].

Applicants should expect armed resistance.

Objectives include:

- Investigate the workshop.
- Recover evidence of Bloodwalker OG trafficking.
- Eliminate or apprehend those responsible.
- Secure any illegal product found on the premises.

Compensation: Reward issued upon successful completion.

Report immediately to Highblade Tower, ask for Ziggy.

---

## [[Highblade Tower]]

Read or paraphrase the following:

> [!Read Aloud]
> *The Highblade Tower is a sturdy brick building with polished brass lanterns flanking its entrance. Green-cloaked officers bustle between offices carrying bundles of reports, confiscated Arcannabis, and evidence boxes sealed with wax.*
> 
> *A goblin wearing a neatly pressed investigator's coat stands balanced on a chair behind the front counter, sorting paperwork into surprisingly tidy piles. Without looking up, he points toward a nearby office.*
> 
> *"If you're here about the candle shop, you're the adventurers I ordered."*
> 
> *Inside the office, maps of the Old Market District cover one wall. Pins, notes, and lengths of colored string connect businesses throughout the neighborhood. Several locations have already been crossed out, leaving only one circled in red.*
> 
> *The goblin hops onto his desk, offering a grin before extending a hand.*
> 
> *"Ziggy Tootokes. Investigator, Tribunal Highblade Coalition. Thanks for answering the bounty."*

### Ziggy Tootokes

Level 3 Goblin Rogue (Scout)

Ziggy Tootokes has earned a reputation for solving cases others overlook. Quick-witted and endlessly curious, he prefers gathering evidence over kicking down doors, but he isn't afraid to get his hands dirty when necessary. His desk is immaculate despite the mountain of case files surrounding it, and he speaks rapidly, often thinking out loud as he pieces together investigations.

Although relaxed and approachable, Ziggy takes Bloodwalker OG very seriously. Every new victim strengthens his resolve to dismantle the organization responsible.

### The Briefing

Ziggy explains the following:

- Bloodwalker OG has become increasingly common throughout Stickyickistan despite being outlawed by the Stickyickistanian Department of Public Health.
- Every attempt to trace the drug back to its producers has reached a dead end.
- Over several weeks of surveillance, THC investigators identified Wick & Wax Candleworks as a common destination for known couriers.
- The workshop continues to sell ordinary candles during the day, giving it the appearance of a struggling but legitimate business.
- Deliveries occur after sunset, when the business should be closed.
- Individuals carrying heavy crates enter the workshop late at night, yet those same crates are never seen leaving, nor do they bare the mark of any known merchant.
- The Coalition believes the workshop is being used as a distribution point, but they have been unable to determine where the product is stored.

> [!Read Aloud]
> *Ziggy rolls a hand-drawn map across the desk, tapping the building with one claw.*
> 
> *"Everything about this place smells wrong. We've watched it for weeks, but no one's carrying crates back out. That means one of two things: they're eating an incredible amount of Arcannabis... or there's more workshop than meets the eye."*
> 
> *He leans back in his chair.*
> 
> *"Find out what's beneath that building. If Bloodwalker OG is there, shut the operation down and bring me whatever records you can find."*

### What Ziggy Knows

If the characters have questions, Ziggy can provide the following information.

- #### Bloodwalker OG
	- Bloodwalker OG is an illegal Arcannabis strain prohibited after investigators discovered it was manufactured using harvested humanoid hearts and other forbidden biological materials.
- #### Wick & Wax Candleworks
	- The business has operated in the Old Market District for decades. Sales have steadily declined, but somehow they manage to stay in business.
- #### The Occupants
	- Investigators have observed at least three regular occupants entering and leaving the workshop, though additional individuals may be inside after dark.
- #### Hidden Storage
	- Ziggy is convinced the workshop conceals a cellar or hidden storage area but has been unable to discover its entrance without conducting an official raid.

## Treasure

The Tribunal Highblade Coalition provides each character with a reward upon mission completion.

## Development

After answering any remaining questions, Ziggy marks the workshop's location on the party's map and wishes them luck.

When the characters arrive at Wick & Wax Candleworks, proceed to Part 2.

---

# Part 2: Wick & Wax Candleworks
*Estimated Duration: 45 Minutes*

![Map](https://content.encounterkit.com/cdn-cgi/image/width=3840,quality=75,format=auto/https://content.encounterkit.com/map/preview/f4f4dcdd80c0028155b6bcd834377216.webp)

In this part, the characters investigate Wick & Wax Candleworks, an aging candle maker's shop in the [[Old Market District]] suspected of concealing an illegal Bloodwalker OG distribution operation. During the day, the building operates as a legitimate business serving ordinary customers. After dark, it becomes the public face of a criminal organization, with shipments arriving and departing under the cover of night.

The workshop conceals two entrances into the hidden cellar below. The first is a trapdoor hidden beneath a crimson rug inside the manager's office. The second is a forgotten smuggler's entrance hidden within an abandoned well in the alley beside the building.

## General Features

Unless otherwise noted, the workshop has the following features.

- **Ceilings.** The workshop ceilings are 12 feet high.
- **Lighting**. During business hours, sunlight enters through the front windows while candles illuminate the work areas. At night, the building is lit entirely by candles and oil lamps.
- **Smell**. The workshop smells strongly of beeswax, rendered tallow, wood smoke, and faint herbal aromas.
- **Bloodwalker Awareness.** Every Cultist, Apprentice Vamplock, and Marek Flint has consumed Bloodwalker OG. They always know the direction of every humanoid within 960 feet. This awareness doesn't reveal identities, numbers, or intentions, only direction. Because of this, the traffickers are rarely surprised by approaching intruders.

---

## Arriving at the Workshop

When the characters arrive at Wick & Wax Candleworks, read or paraphrase the following:

> [!Read Aloud]
> *Nestled among the aging storefronts of the Old Market District stands a narrow brick building with a faded wooden sign hanging above its entrance.*
> 
> *Wick & Wax Candleworks*
> 
> *Finished candles fill the front windows, their warm glow reflecting across the cobblestone street. A thin ribbon of smoke rises from the chimney while the pleasant scent of melted beeswax drifts into the evening air.*
> 
> *Nothing about the little shop appears out of the ordinary.*
> 
> *The building occupies a corner lot. A narrow alley runs along its eastern wall where an old stone well sits beneath weathered wooden planks.*

---

## Visiting During the Day

If the characters arrive while the shop is open, read:

> [!Read Aloud]
> *A brass bell jingles as the front door opens.*
> 
> *The workshop is warm and inviting. Shelves display dozens of finished candles while workbenches are cluttered with molds, carving tools, bundles of wick, and cooling racks. Workers move about their tasks with practiced efficiency as customers browse the shelves.*

The workshop conducts legitimate business during the day.

The Cultists genuinely produce and sell candles while using the storefront to conceal the trafficking operation beneath the building.

Because of Bloodwalker OG, the occupants know the characters are approaching before they enter. Rather than preparing an ambush, they simply continue working while quietly observing the newcomers.

Unless the characters begin searching restricted areas, threaten employees, or openly accuse the workers of criminal activity, the traffickers avoid combat.

---

## Visiting After Dark

If the characters arrive after sunset, read:

> [!Read Aloud]
> *The storefront is dark.*
> 
> *Thick curtains cover the windows, allowing only faint candlelight to escape around their edges.*
> 
> *Somewhere inside, wooden crates scrape across the floor before everything falls silent.*
> 
> *The front door is locked.*

The workshop above serves as the gang's first line of defense.

Because of Bloodwalker OG, the occupants already know humanoids have approached the building and quietly prepare for trouble.

---

## Workshop Occupants

Unless the characters enter through the hidden well, the following creatures occupy the workshop.

- Marek Flint, Vampirate Mage
- 1 Apprentice Vamplock
- 2 Cultists

The Cultists work openly on the production floor.

The Apprentice Vamplock assists with bookkeeping and shipment preparation.

Marek Flint remains in the northeast office reviewing shipment manifests.

---

### Marek Flint

Vampirate Mage

Marek Flint was once a respected alchemist whose fascination with rare Arcannabis strains slowly consumed him. After embracing undeath, he now oversees one of the city's largest Bloodwalker OG distribution houses.

Marek is calm, patient, and exceptionally organized. He speaks with measured confidence and treats every conversation as though negotiating a business contract. Violence is simply another expense to be managed.

Unlike the Cultists who serve him, Marek has little interest in fanaticism. He believes Bloodwalker OG is the future of Arcannabis and considers morality an obstacle to progress.

His office is immaculate. Every shipment, payment, and customer is carefully documented in ledgers arranged with obsessive precision.

---

## Searching the Workshop

Characters searching the workshop can discover the following.

- ### Showroom
	- The candles are genuine and expertly crafted. Nothing immediately suggests criminal activity.
- ### Workshop
	- The workbenches contain ordinary candle-making equipment. A successful DC 13 Wisdom (Medicine) check notices faint traces of dried blood on one recently cleaned carving knife.
- ### Storage
	- Most crates contain legitimate supplies. Several barrels feature cleverly constructed false bottoms capable of concealing packages of Bloodwalker OG.
- ### Office
	- Marek Flint's office is immaculate. A polished oak desk dominates the room, its surface free of clutter save for neatly stacked ledgers, an inkpot, and a brass candle holder. Shelves line the walls, filled with years of business records documenting the workshop's legitimate candle sales.
	- A large crimson rug covers most of the wooden floor.
	- A character who succeeds on a **DC 12 Wisdom (Perception) or DC 12 Intelligence (Investigation)** check notices faint scrape marks around the edges of the rug. Pulling it aside reveals a heavy wooden trapdoor fitted with a recessed iron pull ring. The trapdoor opens onto a sturdy wooden ladder descending into the hidden cellar below.
	- A successful **DC 14 Intelligence (Investigation)** check of the desk reveals a false compartment concealed within one of the drawers. Inside is a folded letter sealed with crimson wax bearing the image of a circle enclosing three parallel vertical lines.
	- This is the first evidence the characters uncover linking the operation to an organization known as The Bloodline. It also identifies Wick & Wax Candleworks as Branch Seven.
	- The letter reads:

> Branch Seven,
> 
> Your latest shipment has been received without incident. Continue maintaining normal business during daylight hours. The workshop remains an effective cover for distribution operations.
> 
> The Tribunal Highblade Coalition continues pursuing local traffickers and remains unaware of our wider network.
> 
> Burn this correspondence after reading.
> 
> —The Bloodline

- ### Strongbox
	- A sturdy iron strongbox rests beneath the desk.
	- The lock can be opened with a successful DC 15 Dexterity check using thieves' tools or forced open with a successful DC 20 Strength (Athletics) check.
	- Inside are:
		- 185 gp
		- Three blood-red garnets, each worth 50 gp
		- A silver signet ring engraved with the same emblem found on the letter—a circle enclosing three parallel vertical lines
		- A Portable Hole, carefully folded and wrapped in waxed linen
	- Tied to the Portable Hole is a small inventory tag written in a precise hand.

> **Branch Property**
> 
> Destination: Branch Three
> 
> Handle With Care.
> 
> Unauthorized use is punishable by forfeiture.
> 
> —The Bloodline

- ### The Hidden Well
	- The abandoned well in the eastern alley conceals a second entrance into the cellar.
	- A successful **DC 12 Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation)** check notices that the weathered planks covering the well have been moved recently.
	- Removing the planks reveals an iron ladder descending into darkness.
	- The ladder leads directly into the cellar, bypassing the workshop entirely.
	- Characters entering this way avoid the surface encounter.

---

## Combat

If combat begins inside the workshop, the Cultists immediately engage the intruders while the Apprentice Vamplock supports them with spells from behind cover. Marek Flint enters the battle from his office at the beginning of the first round. He calmly closes his ledger before joining the fight.

Read or paraphrase:

> [!Read Aloud]
> *A door swings open.*
> 
> *A pale man in immaculate dark robes steps into the workshop carrying himself with the confidence of someone greeting late customers rather than armed intruders.*
> 
> *He glances over the scene, sighs softly, and brushes an imaginary speck of dust from one sleeve.*
> 
> *"This is becoming expensive."*

Marek fights intelligently, preferring to remain behind his subordinates while using his spells to control the battlefield.

When reduced to half his hit points or fewer, Marek abandons the workshop.

Without revealing the hidden trapdoor, he grabs the Strongbox from under his desk then casts Dimension Door, teleporting into the cellar below where he prepares a final defense.

The Cultists continue fighting, buying time for their master.

Alternatively, if the characters entered through the hidden well, Marek remains in his office until he hears combat below in Part 3. He then descends into the cellar through the trapdoor at the start of the second round of combat.

## Development

If the characters defeat the workshop occupants, they eventually discover the concealed trapdoor beneath Marek's office, or they take too long and Marek escapes with his henchmen and the product.

If they instead entered through the hidden well, they bypass the workshop entirely. The Cultists remain above while Marek is forced to descend into the cellar after hearing combat below.

In either case, proceed to Part 3: The Hidden Cellar.

---

# Part 3: The Hidden Cellar
*Estimated Duration: 45 Minutes*

![Map](cellar.png)

Hidden beneath Wick & Wax Candleworks lies Branch Seven's distribution center. Here, Bloodwalker OG is weighed, packaged, and prepared for shipment throughout Stickyickistan. Unlike the orderly storefront above, the cellar serves only one purpose—keeping The Bloodline's illicit trade moving.

If the characters discovered the hidden well, they enter through area C2. Otherwise, they descend from Marek's office into C1.

## General Features

Unless otherwise noted, the cellar has the following features.

- **Ceilings.** The ceilings are 8 feet high.
- **Lighting**. Hooded lanterns provide dim light throughout the cellar.
- **Walls**. Rough stone walls are reinforced with heavy timber supports.
- **Smell**. Damp earth, mildew, lamp oil, and the pungent aroma of processed Bloodwalker OG fill the air.

---

## C1. Trapdoor Entrance

A sturdy wooden ladder descends from the trapdoor above into a small storage alcove stacked with empty barrels, spare crates, and coils of rope.

If the characters enter from the workshop, they arrive here.

If Marek escaped the battle above, he appears here after casting Dimension Door, clutching the strongbox from his office before moving toward area C3.

---

## C2. Smuggler's Well

A rusted iron ladder climbs nearly 30 feet through a narrow stone shaft before disappearing into darkness above.

The abandoned well provides a discreet route for moving contraband into and out of the cellar without passing through the storefront.

Characters entering through the well begin the encounter here.

---

## C3. Distribution Floor

Read or paraphrase the following:

> [!Read Aloud]
> *Long wooden tables divide the largest chamber of the cellar. Bundles of dried crimson Arcannabis lie beside scales, sealing wax, twine, and stacks of shipping crates. Lantern light flickers across dozens of neatly wrapped packages awaiting collection.*

This is no hidden laboratory. It is a warehouse built to move product.

Unless they have already been defeated, the following creatures occupy this room:

- 1 Apprentice Vamplock
- 2 Cultists

The cultists are packaging shipments while the Apprentice Vamplock oversees the evening's work.

Because of Bloodwalker OG, they are already aware that humanoids have entered the cellar and immediately prepare to defend the operation.

### Crates

Most crates contain ordinary candles used to maintain the appearance of a legitimate business.

A successful DC 13 Intelligence (Investigation) check discovers that several crates contain false bottoms concealing tightly wrapped packages of Bloodwalker OG.

### Shipment Records

Shipping manifests cover one of the worktables.

Each shipment is addressed only to numbered branches.

No destinations or names are recorded.

---

### Marek Arrives

Marek joins the encounter under either of the following circumstances:

- He escaped from the workshop using Dimension Door, arriving through area C1 with the strongbox.
- The characters entered through the hidden well and combat breaks out in the cellar.

Read or paraphrase:

> [!Read Aloud]
> *Heavy footsteps echo overhead, followed by the crash of a trapdoor opening.*
> 
> *Marek Flint descends quickly, an iron strongbox tucked securely beneath one arm.*
> 
> *His eyes dart briefly toward the well before settling on the intruders.*
> 
> *"You've already cost me tonight's shipment."*
> 
> *He sighs, adjusts his grip on the strongbox, and raises a hand crackling with necrotic energy.*
> 
> *"I won't allow you to cost me the rest."*

Roll initiative for Marek if he has not already acted.

### Marek's Goal

- Marek has no intention of dying beneath the workshop.
- His priority is protecting Bloodline property.
- If an opportunity presents itself, Marek attempts to fight his way to the smuggler's well and escape with the strongbox.
- He only abandons the strongbox if doing so is necessary to preserve his own unlife.

---

### Shadows

Marek's Energy Drain creates Shadows as described in his stat block.

If a humanoid is slain by this attack, its shadow tears free from the corpse and immediately joins the battle under Marek's control.

---

## C4. Workers' Quarters

Simple wooden bunks line the walls of this cramped chamber. Footlockers, hooks for work aprons, and shelves containing cheap cookware suggest that several workers live here for days at a time.

A table near the center of the room is littered with playing cards, clay pipes, and empty mugs.

Searching the room uncovers no treasure, though a successful DC 12 Intelligence (Investigation) check reveals a work schedule pinned beside the door. The roster rotates workers between the storefront, the cellar, and overnight delivery shifts, suggesting Branch Seven employs far more personnel than the defenders encountered today.

---

## Development

If Marek escapes through the well, the characters have successfully dismantled Branch Seven's distribution center, though its manager remains at large.

If Marek is defeated, the characters recover the strongbox along with any Bloodline property he carried from the office.

Without its leadership and distribution network, Branch Seven ceases operation.

The Bloodwalker OG stored within the cellar can be confiscated or destroyed, preventing countless doses from reaching the streets of Stickyickistan.

The evidence recovered from Marek's office confirms that Branch Seven is only one small part of a much larger criminal syndicate known as The Bloodline. Returning this evidence to Ziggy Tootokes completes the investigation and provides the Tribunal Highblade Coalition with its first tangible lead into the organization.

# Conclusion

Read or paraphrase the following:

Ziggy carefully studies the recovered correspondence before letting out a slow whistle.

"Branch Seven..."

"For months we've been chasing dealers and smugglers, thinking we'd eventually reach whoever was calling the shots."

He folds the letter and slips it into his satchel.

"Turns out we've only been pruning branches."

Ziggy smiles and extends a hand.

"Excellent work. The Tribunal Highblade Coalition finally has something real to investigate."

Whether Marek Flint escaped or was defeated, the destruction of Branch Seven deals a significant blow to The Bloodline's operations in the Old Market District.

Unfortunately, the evidence recovered from his office suggests the organization extends far beyond a single candle shop.

## Rewards

Upon returning to Ziggy Tootokes, each character receives the promised bounty for dismantling Branch Seven.

The characters also recover the following treasure during the adventure.

- 185 gp
- Three garnets worth 50 gp each
- A silver signet ring engraved with The Bloodline's symbol
- Any mundane equipment recovered from defeated enemies

## Treasure Bundles

At the conclusion of the adventure, award one Treasure Bundle to the party. Roll on the table below or choose the result that best fits your campaign.

|   |   |
|---|---|
|Options|Treasure Bundle|
|1|Portable Hole. Wrapped in waxed linen with an inventory tag reading Branch Property – Destination: Branch Three.|
|2|Alchemist's Cache. A sturdy leather case containing an Alchemy Jug, and 75 gp.|
|3|Explorer's Kit. A beautifully crafted Lantern of Revealing, a Potion of Greater Healing.|

---

## Story Award

## Friend of Ziggy

The characters have earned the trust and respect of Ziggy Tootokes, Investigator of the Tribunal Highblade Coalition.

Whenever the characters seek information regarding criminal activity, smuggling operations, or Arcannabis trafficking within Stickyickistan, Ziggy is willing to share what he knows or point them toward new leads, provided doing so does not compromise an ongoing investigation.

If Ziggy appears in a future adventure, he greets the characters as trusted associates and does his best to assist them.

---

# Experience

Characters who complete this adventure earn 1,350 XP, approximately enough to advance a 3rd-level character halfway to 4th level.

---

# Dungeon Master Aid: Rumors

Before beginning this adventure, the characters may gather information throughout Stickyickistan.

A party may purchase up to three Copper Rumors, two Silver Rumors, or one Gold Rumor before starting part 2.

Each rumor requires spending the associated coin and represents several hours of asking questions, buying drinks, or consulting contacts.

The Dungeon Master may roll randomly or choose a rumor appropriate to the campaign.

---

## Copper Rumors (1 cp)

Source: The Regulars

The cheapest information comes from dockworkers, laborers, merchants, bartenders, and other everyday folk. Most of what they know comes from gossip and personal observation. While generally reliable, these rumors often lack important context.

|   |   |
|---|---|
|d12|Rumor|
|1|Wick & Wax Candleworks has operated in the Old Market District longer than anyone can remember.|
|2|The shop makes excellent candles, but the workers keep mostly to themselves.|
|3|Wagons occasionally arrive long after the shop has closed for the evening.|
|4|The smell drifting from the workshop after dark isn't quite beeswax.|
|5|The manager rarely speaks with customers, leaving the workers to handle most sales.|
|6|The alley beside the shop is unusually quiet after sunset.|
|7|Some folks swear the building has an old cellar dating back before the city expanded.|
|8|The workers always seem to have plenty of coin despite making candles for a living.|
|9|A few neighboring merchants claim the workshop receives more deliveries than it should.|
|10|Children tell stories about hearing voices echoing from the old well beside the shop.|
|11|Nobody seems to know who actually owns Wick & Wax Candleworks anymore.|
|12|The shop closes at dusk, but lights can often be seen burning inside well into the night.|

---

## Silver Rumors (1 sp)

Source: Penny "Two-Coppers" Bramble

A retired halfling fence turned neighborhood broker, Penny earns a comfortable living trading information instead of stolen goods. She knows which guards look the other way, which businesses pay protection, and who has recently come into unexpected wealth.

Penny never guarantees her information—but she refuses to sell rumors she doesn't believe.

|   |   |
|---|---|
|d8|Rumor|
|1|The workshop is perfectly legitimate during the day. Whatever is happening there occurs after business hours.|
|2|Marek Flint spends most of his time working from a private office toward the rear of the building.|
|3|Workers have been seen entering through the front door and leaving by the eastern alley late at night.|
|4|The abandoned well beside the workshop predates the building itself.|
|5|Large deliveries almost always arrive after sunset.|
|6|More people work at Wick & Wax than a candle shop should reasonably employ.|
|7|Customers are never permitted beyond the showroom and workshop floor.|
|8|Coalition investigators have watched the shop for months but have never found enough evidence to justify a raid.|

---

## Gold Rumors (1 gp)

Source: Ziggy Tootokes

As an investigator with the Tribunal Highblade Coalition, Ziggy has access to confidential reports, informants, and evidence unavailable to the general public. He only shares this information with adventurers he believes can be trusted.

|   |   |
|---|---|
|d6|Rumor|
|1|Coalition surveillance strongly suggests the abandoned well connects to the cellar beneath the workshop.|
|2|Marek Flint is known for protecting Bloodline assets above all else. If forced to retreat, he'll likely attempt to escape with whatever valuables he can carry.|
|3|Bloodwalker OG grants its users an uncanny awareness of nearby humanoids. Stealth alone won't be enough to catch them by surprise.|
|4|Wick & Wax Candleworks appears to be a distribution point, not the source of Bloodwalker OG. Someone else is supplying the operation.|
|5|Coalition informants believe Marek keeps his most important records in his office rather than the cellar below.|
|6|Criminal correspondence refers to Wick & Wax as Branch Seven, implying it is only one part of a much larger network.|

*A Stickyickistan Adventure for Four to Five 3rd-Level Characters*

Crimson Candleworks is optimized for five 3rd-level characters. This adventure should be completed in four hours or less.

The adventure takes place in the city of [[Stickyickistan]], where a seemingly ordinary candle maker's workshop conceals an illegal Bloodwalker OG distribution operation beneath its floorboards. Hired by the [[Tribunal Highblade Coalition]], the characters investigate the business, uncover its hidden cellar, and dismantle the criminal enterprise operating below.

# Intro

## Adjusting Encounters

If you have fewer than five players, a group of inexperienced players, or characters who are poorly equipped, the adventure may suggest adjusting certain encounters to be less challenging. If your players are experienced or have particularly optimized characters, the adventure may also suggest ways to increase the difficulty.

Consult with your players before beginning if adjustments seem appropriate. You can always modify encounters during play to provide the most enjoyable experience for your table.

---

## Key Plot Points

The following information is key to the adventure's story.

**Part 1:** [[The Rolling Papers]]. The characters discover a bounty posted by the Tribunal Highblade Coalition seeking adventurers willing to raid a suspected Bloodwalker OG distribution site operating beneath a candle maker's workshop.

**Part 2:** Wick & Wax Candleworks. The characters investigate the workshop, discover the concealed trapdoor hidden beneath a worn rug, and descend into the cellar where the operation is based. There they confront the undead traffickers responsible for distributing the illegal strain.

**Conclusion:** Another Candle Extinguished. After dismantling the operation, the characters recover evidence pointing toward the unknown producers of Bloodwalker OG before returning to the Tribunal Highblade Coalition to claim their reward.

---

## Preparation

Before running the adventure, prepare as follows:

- **Step 1**. Read the Adventure Background section.
- **Step 2**. Review any rules from the Player's Handbook, Dungeon Master's Guide, or Homebrew that may come into play.
- **Step 3**. Bookmark the creature stat blocks needed for the adventure or have them readily available.
- **Step 4.** Familiarize yourself with the [[Arcannabis System Rework]], and the Cooking rules in [[Heliana's Guide to Monster Hunting]], so you know why and how Bloodwalker OG works the way it does.

The following stat blocks are used in this adventure:

- [[Apprentice Vamplock]]
- [[Cultist]]
- [[Shadow]]
- [[Vampirate Mage]]

> [!Read Aloud]
> Text that appears in a box like this is intended to be read aloud or paraphrased for the players when their characters first arrive at a location or under the circumstances described.

---

## Key NPCs

|                      |                                                                                                                      |                       |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| Name                 | Role                                                                                                                 | Stat Block            |
| [[Ziggy Tootokes]]   | Coalition agent overseeing the bounty                                                                                | Level 3 Rogue (Scout) |
| [[Marek Flint]]      | Manager of the Wick & Wax Candleshop. Also a member of a gang called The Bloodline. He leads this distribution cell. | Vampirate Mage        |
| Apprentice Vamplocks | Undead assistants managing the cellar                                                                                | Apprentice Vamplock   |

---

## Content Warning

Body horror, illicit drug trafficking, undead, murder, and references to harvested humanoid remains.

---

## Adventure Background

[[Arcannabis]] has long been one of Stickyickistan's most valuable commodities. While legitimate growers operate under strict regulations, criminal organizations continue to produce illicit strains using dangerous and prohibited ingredients.

Among the most infamous is [[Bloodwalker OG]], a strain outlawed by the [[Stickyickistanian Department of Public Health]] after investigators discovered it was manufactured using harvested humanoid hearts, celestial remains, and other forbidden monster components.

Responsibility for enforcing that ban falls to the [[Tribunal Highblade Coalition]] (THC). For months, Coalition investigators have pursued dealers distributing Bloodwalker OG throughout the city, but every trail has ended before reaching the source.

Their investigation finally uncovered a consistent pattern. Couriers supplying local dealers repeatedly visited an aging candle maker's workshop tucked away among the city's older commercial district. Although the storefront appeared to conduct legitimate business during the day, surveillance revealed unusual deliveries after dark and an impossible amount of traffic for a struggling artisan.

Unable to obtain sufficient evidence for a lawful raid, Coalition investigators posted a public bounty seeking capable adventurers willing to investigate the property.

Unknown to the authorities, the candle workshop serves as little more than a façade. Beneath a faded rug inside the workshop lies a concealed trapdoor leading into a cellar where Bloodwalker OG is packaged, stored, and distributed throughout the city. Shipments arrive from hidden cultivation sites elsewhere in Stickyickistan, while victims murdered during the operation have their hearts harvested and returned to the growers for future production.

The cellar is commanded by a Vampirate and several undead accomplices, all of whom have consumed Bloodwalker OG and now zealously protect the operation. If the workshop is exposed, the Coalition hopes the evidence recovered below will reveal who truly controls the Bloodwalker OG supply.

---

# Part 1: The Rolling Papers
*Estimated Duration: 30 Minutes*

In this part, the characters discover a bounty advertisement in The Rolling Papers, Stickyickistan's most widely circulated newspaper. Reporting to the Tribunal Highblade Coalition (THC), they meet Investigator Ziggy Tootokes, who briefs them on an ongoing Bloodwalker OG investigation before sending them to raid a suspected distribution site concealed beneath a candle maker's workshop.

## Adventure Hook

While reading the latest edition of The Rolling Papers, the characters notice a bounty posted in the newspaper's Bounties & Advertisements section.

Hand the players the following notice or read it aloud.

---

### BOUNTY POSTED

#### Tribunal Highblade Coalition

INVESTIGATION & RAID AUTHORIZED

The Tribunal Highblade Coalition seeks capable adventurers to investigate a suspected illegal Arcannabis distribution operation believed to be beneath Wick & Wax Candleworks, located in the [[Old Market District]].

Applicants should expect armed resistance.

Objectives include:

- Investigate the workshop.
- Recover evidence of Bloodwalker OG trafficking.
- Eliminate or apprehend those responsible.
- Secure any illegal product found on the premises.

Compensation: Reward issued upon successful completion.

Report immediately to Highblade Tower, ask for Ziggy.

---

## [[Highblade Tower]]

Read or paraphrase the following:

> [!Read Aloud]
> *The Highblade Tower is a sturdy brick building with polished brass lanterns flanking its entrance. Green-cloaked officers bustle between offices carrying bundles of reports, confiscated Arcannabis, and evidence boxes sealed with wax.*
> 
> *A goblin wearing a neatly pressed investigator's coat stands balanced on a chair behind the front counter, sorting paperwork into surprisingly tidy piles. Without looking up, he points toward a nearby office.*
> 
> *"If you're here about the candle shop, you're the adventurers I ordered."*
> 
> *Inside the office, maps of the Old Market District cover one wall. Pins, notes, and lengths of colored string connect businesses throughout the neighborhood. Several locations have already been crossed out, leaving only one circled in red.*
> 
> *The goblin hops onto his desk, offering a grin before extending a hand.*
> 
> *"Ziggy Tootokes. Investigator, Tribunal Highblade Coalition. Thanks for answering the bounty."*

### Ziggy Tootokes

Level 3 Goblin Rogue (Scout)

Ziggy Tootokes has earned a reputation for solving cases others overlook. Quick-witted and endlessly curious, he prefers gathering evidence over kicking down doors, but he isn't afraid to get his hands dirty when necessary. His desk is immaculate despite the mountain of case files surrounding it, and he speaks rapidly, often thinking out loud as he pieces together investigations.

Although relaxed and approachable, Ziggy takes Bloodwalker OG very seriously. Every new victim strengthens his resolve to dismantle the organization responsible.

### The Briefing

Ziggy explains the following:

- Bloodwalker OG has become increasingly common throughout Stickyickistan despite being outlawed by the Stickyickistanian Department of Public Health.
- Every attempt to trace the drug back to its producers has reached a dead end.
- Over several weeks of surveillance, THC investigators identified Wick & Wax Candleworks as a common destination for known couriers.
- The workshop continues to sell ordinary candles during the day, giving it the appearance of a struggling but legitimate business.
- Deliveries occur after sunset, when the business should be closed.
- Individuals carrying heavy crates enter the workshop late at night, yet those same crates are never seen leaving, nor do they bare the mark of any known merchant.
- The Coalition believes the workshop is being used as a distribution point, but they have been unable to determine where the product is stored.

> [!Read Aloud]
> *Ziggy rolls a hand-drawn map across the desk, tapping the building with one claw.*
> 
> *"Everything about this place smells wrong. We've watched it for weeks, but no one's carrying crates back out. That means one of two things: they're eating an incredible amount of Arcannabis... or there's more workshop than meets the eye."*
> 
> *He leans back in his chair.*
> 
> *"Find out what's beneath that building. If Bloodwalker OG is there, shut the operation down and bring me whatever records you can find."*

### What Ziggy Knows

If the characters have questions, Ziggy can provide the following information.

- #### Bloodwalker OG
	- Bloodwalker OG is an illegal Arcannabis strain prohibited after investigators discovered it was manufactured using harvested humanoid hearts and other forbidden biological materials.
- #### Wick & Wax Candleworks
	- The business has operated in the Old Market District for decades. Sales have steadily declined, but somehow they manage to stay in business.
- #### The Occupants
	- Investigators have observed at least three regular occupants entering and leaving the workshop, though additional individuals may be inside after dark.
- #### Hidden Storage
	- Ziggy is convinced the workshop conceals a cellar or hidden storage area but has been unable to discover its entrance without conducting an official raid.

## Treasure

The Tribunal Highblade Coalition provides each character with a reward upon mission completion.

## Development

After answering any remaining questions, Ziggy marks the workshop's location on the party's map and wishes them luck.

When the characters arrive at Wick & Wax Candleworks, proceed to Part 2.
